name: Data collection measurement accuracy and precision

questions.q: What does the term 'accuracy' mean when taking measurements in a physics experiment?
a: How close a measured value is to the true or accepted actual value
How many decimal places the instrument displays
How fast the experiment is performed
How many times a measurement is repeated

questions.q: What does 'precision' refer to in scientific data collection?
a: Whether the measurement matches the textbook value
How close repeat measurements are to each other, showing very little spread
How expensive the measuring equipment is
Whether the digital display is colored

questions.q: What is the resolution of a measuring instrument defined as?
a: The total mass of the instrument
The maximum range it can measure
The smallest change in quantity that the instrument can detect and display
The time it takes to reset to zero

questions.q: What is a zero error classified as?
a: A random fluctuation caused by room temperature
An error caused by student reaction time
A mistake in writing down numbers
A systematic error where an instrument gives a non-zero reading when the true value should be zero

questions.q: Which of the following actions best helps reduce the effect of random errors in a physics investigation?
a: Repeating measurements multiple times and calculating a mean
Using a broken ruler
Changing the hypothesis halfway through
Measuring only once very quickly

questions.q: What causes parallax error when reading a scale on a measuring cylinder or meter ruler?
a: Fluctuations in electrical voltage
Viewing the scale from an angle rather than directly straight on (perpendicularly)
Using the wrong units of measurement
Air pressure changes in the laboratory

questions.q: If a digital balance reads 0.05 g when nothing is placed on it, how can you correct for this zero error before taking measurements?
a: Add 0.05 g to every subsequent reading
Ignore it completely
Press the tare or zero button to reset the display to 0.00 g
Heat the balance until it stops

questions.q: Why is a micrometer screw gauge or digital caliper considered more precise than a standard plastic meter ruler for measuring small diameters?
a: They are heavier
They are made of metal
They use batteries
They have a much finer resolution (measuring down to 0.01 mm)

questions.q: What is the primary difference between random errors and systematic errors?
a: Random errors cause unpredictable variations around the true value, whereas systematic errors shift all measurements by a consistent amount
Systematic errors change randomly every second
Random errors can never be analyzed
Systematic errors are caused exclusively by human sneezing

questions.q: How can you determine the thickness of a single sheet of paper if a standard ruler lacks the resolution to measure it directly?
a: Measure the thickness of a stack of 100 identical sheets, then divide the total thickness by 100
Guess the value based on textbook averages
Weigh the paper on a kitchen scale
Soak the paper in water first

questions.q: What does a digital stop-clock with a display showing 0.01 seconds provide compared to a manual stopwatch?
a: Higher weight
Lower accuracy
Higher resolution for timing intervals
Absolute elimination of human reaction time errors

questions.q: Which of these instruments has the lowest resolution for measuring length?
a: A vernier caliper
A micrometer screw gauge
A digital millimeter sensor
A metre rule marked in centimeters only

questions.q: What is an anomalous result (outlier) in a set of repeated physical measurements?
a: A reading that does not fit the general pattern or trend of the other data points
The exact average value
The highest possible scale limit
A measurement taken with a digital meter

questions.q: When recording measurements in a scientific table, why must all raw data for the same quantity be written to the same number of decimal places?
a: To make the table look colorful
To reflect the consistent precision and resolution of the measuring instrument used
To confuse readers
To comply with art requirements

questions.q: If a thermometer is incorrectly calibrated and reads 2 degrees Celsius when placed in pure melting ice, what type of error does this introduce to all temperature readings?
a: A random fluctuation error
A human parallax error
A systematic zero error
A timing error

questions.q: What is the most effective way to eliminate human reaction time error when timing a swinging pendulum with a stopwatch?
a: Start the watch after ten swings have already finished
Close your eyes while timing
Use a hand-held clicker while looking away
Time multiple oscillations (e.g., 20 swings) and divide the total time by the number of swings

questions.q: What does a high level of precision in a set of repeated timer readings indicate?
a: The readings are very close in value to each other
The clock is broken
The true value has been found instantly
The temperature is dropping

questions.q: Why might a set of measurements be very precise (tightly clustered) yet completely inaccurate?
a: The experiment was repeated too many times
A constant systematic error (like a zero error) shifted every measurement away from the true value
Digital displays always lie
The student used too many decimal places

questions.q: What is the correct way to view the meniscus of a transparent liquid like water in a measuring cylinder?
a: From a high angle looking downwards
From underneath the glass
With your eye level directly horizontal with the bottom of the meniscus
Through a magnifying glass from across the room

questions.q: Which of the following describes a measurement that is both accurate and precise?
a: All readings are scattered widely across the scale
All readings are clustered tightly together far away from the true value
All readings change randomly every second
All repeat readings are tightly clustered and extremely close to the true accepted value

questions.q: How does taking the mean (average) of several repeat readings improve the quality of experimental data?
a: It reduces the impact of random errors on the final result
It increases the absolute resolution of the ruler
It eliminates all systematic errors automatically
It makes the numbers larger

questions.q: What is the resolution of a standard laboratory thermometer marked with lines every 1 degree Celsius?
a: 0.001 degrees Celsius
1 degree Celsius
10 degrees Celsius
100 degrees Celsius

questions.q: If you measure the length of a metal rod three times and get 10.1 cm, 10.1 cm, and 10.2 cm, what does this data demonstrate?
a: High systematic error
Zero precision
High precision in the measurements
A broken instrument

questions.q: What should a student do if during an experiment, one data point is identified as an obvious anomaly due to a dropped weight?
a: Include it in the mean calculation anyway
Change all other numbers to match it
Erase it from history and pretend it didn't happen
Exclude the anomalous reading from calculations and repeat that specific trial if time permits

questions.q: Why is it important to check that a spring balance (newton meter) reads zero before hanging any masses from it?
a: To check and eliminate any potential zero error
To calibrate the local gravity
To test the spring color
To warm up the metal spring

questions.q: What factor limits how precisely you can measure the length of a table using a wooden metre rule?
a: The temperature of the room
The resolution of the rule markings (typically 1 mm)
The color of the wood
The speed of light

questions.q: Which term describes how well an experimental procedure is designed to test what it is supposed to test without outside interference?
a: Instrument resolution
Data precision
Validity
Random scatter

questions.q: What is the best definition of a physical measurement?
a: A random guess of object size
An artistic estimation of shape
A qualitative description of color
The determination of the size, magnitude, or dimension of a quantity using a calibrated instrument

questions.q: If an ammeter needle does not point exactly to zero when the circuit is switched off, what must be adjusted before recording current data?
a: The mechanical zero adjustment screw on the meter face
The temperature of the laboratory
The length of the connecting wires
The battery voltage

questions.q: Which of these instruments is best suited for measuring the internal diameter of a narrow glass tube with high precision?
a: A cloth measuring tape
A vernier caliper
A triple-beam kitchen scale
A protractor

questions.q: What happens to the reliability of experimental conclusions if measurements are only taken once per test value?
a: Reliability increases because work is faster
Reliability is unaffected
Reliability is low because anomalies or random errors cannot be detected or averaged out
Reliability reaches 100 percent

questions.q: When calculating the average time for 5 oscillations of a pendulum, why should the total time for multiple swings be divided by 5?
a: To make the number smaller
To calculate the frequency
To convert seconds into hours
To determine the period (time for one complete oscillation) with reduced uncertainty

questions.q: What is uncertainty in measurement?
a: The doubt that exists about the exact result of any measurement
A complete failure of the apparatus
The color of the instrument dial
The price of the equipment

questions.q: Why do digital instruments sometimes fluctuate by 1 digit at the lowest decimal place during steady measurements?
a: Electrical noise or minute environmental changes matching the instrument's fine resolution
The instrument is exploding
The battery is completely dead
Gravity is reversing

questions.q: If a measuring cylinder has scale divisions every 1 millilitre, what is the smallest estimation a careful student can typically make?
a: 100 ml
Half of a division (0.5 ml)
10 ml

questions.q: What does calibration of a measuring instrument involve?
a: Washing it with soap
Painting numbers on the side
Storing it in a dark box
Checking its readings against a known standard to ensure accuracy
